candidate.blueprint_locator: 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan, Reduction of Risk Potential, printed p.13 / PDF p.17
candidate.educational_objective: Interpret elevated LDH as a nonspecific tissue-injury/disease marker rather than a diagnosis by itself.

options.A: LDH is a nonspecific marker that can rise with injury or disease involving several tissues, so the result requires clinical correlation
options.B: LDH elevation uniquely diagnoses one specific cancer
options.C: LDH is useful only for kidney disease
options.D: Any elevated LDH proves acute myocardial infarction

candidate.rationale: Mayo Clinic Laboratories notes that LDH is present in many tissues and can be elevated in numerous conditions involving the heart, liver, muscle, kidney, lung, and blood. It is too nonspecific for diagnosis of cancer and has been superseded by troponin for myocardial infarction assessment. An elevated LDH therefore requires clinical correlation.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Supports broad tissue distribution and nonspecific LDH elevation across multiple disease processes.
candidate.stem: A client has an elevated serum lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) result. Which interpretation is most accurate?

warning: Technical candidate selection only. This file is not clinical audit evidence and does not establish PASS or FAIL.
